mostWorthwhile.text: Building the epidermal barrier was worthwhile because its description connected lipids and outer cells to water retention and renewal by deeper cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to join the epidermis and dermis was confusing: the layers seemed like a natural pair, but the need to vascularise the dermis first was not apparent.

surprise.text: The epidermal barrier could not combine with anything initially, but became compatible once the dermis had blood vessels.

arbitrary.text: Requiring vessels in the dermis before joining the two layers felt like an unexplained assembly constraint, even though vascularising the dermis itself made sense.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: the constructions connect anatomy to functions such as water retention and sensation, though I would hope for clearer clues about assembly order.
